1. The animation shows a historical comparison of buying and renting in the US. It uses a grid of 307 blocks, one for each month from January 1991 to July 2016. The headline says "about 3 in 4 (75.6%)", and a label says "75 of 307". The sources are FHFA home prices, BLS rents and Freddie Mac mortgage rates. A tag marks the whole thing as "ILLUSTRATIVE".

2. Very little changes. The grid and headline stay the same across all six frames. The "75 of 307" label shows up in frame 3. A line appears in frames 5 and 6 saying "counted: interest · tax · insurance · repairs · buying and selling". A darker band of blocks in the middle of the grid stays in place throughout. It may be the highlighted 75, but the frames don't say so.

3. The frames don't say which side the 75.6% belongs to, and the 75 of 307 figure doesn't match 75.6% of 307. The darker band is about 75 blocks wide, though, so the 75.6% may describe the highlighted group. I can't tell whether it counts months where buying beat renting or months where renting did. The note about what was counted suggests the comparison included the full costs of owning, not only the mortgage payment. The small print says this is US history and not a forecast.

4. The frames give no advice. A viewer could only guess a conclusion, and it would be a weak one, because the direction of the 75.6% isn't shown.

5. Answer to 4: none. The animation didn't state any advice, and I haven't added any of my own.
